name: API Gateway Memory Leak Recovery
description: Diagnose and recover from memory leaks in the API Gateway service
diagnostic_steps: Check current memory usage: kubectl top pods -n production
Review recent deployments: kubectl rollout history deployment/api-gateway
Examine heap dumps: kubectl exec -it <pod> -- jmap -histo:live <pid>
Check for memory trends in monitoring: look for continuously increasing RSS
Review application logs for GC pressure or OutOfMemoryError
remediation_steps: Rollback the latest deployment: kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway
Restart affected pods: kubectl rollout restart deployment/api-gateway
Monitor memory usage post-restart
Alert engineering team to investigate the memory leak in the rolled-back version
Create a hotfix branch and prepare a patched release
rollback: If rollback fails, scale up replicas temporarily and drain the leaking pods
success_criteria: No OOM events in the past 10 minutes

name: High CPU Investigation
description: Investigate and mitigate high CPU utilization on any service
diagnostic_steps: Identify top CPU consumers: kubectl top pods --sort-by=cpu
Check for recent deployments or config changes
Profile application: check for hot code paths
Review incoming traffic patterns
Check for runaway processes or loops
remediation_steps: If deployment-related: rollback last deployment
If traffic spike: enable rate limiting
Horizontal scale: kubectl scale deployment/<name> --replicas=<n>
Kill runaway processes if identified
Enable CPU throttling as temporary measure
rollback: Restore previous replica count and deployment version

name: Database Timeout Recovery
description: Recover from database connection timeouts and connection pool exhaustion
diagnostic_steps: Check active database connections: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity
Identify long-running queries: SELECT * FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'active' ORDER BY duration DESC
Check connection pool metrics in application
Review database server resource utilization
Check network connectivity between app and database
remediation_steps: Kill long-running blocking queries: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid)
Restart connection pool: restart application pods
If connection pool exhausted: increase pool size temporarily
Scale read replicas if read-heavy load
Enable query timeout for long-running queries
success_criteria: No timeout errors in application logs
Query response times within normal range

name: Slow Query Investigation
description: Investigate and optimize slow database queries causing performance degradation
diagnostic_steps: Enable slow query log: SET GLOBAL slow_query_log = 'ON'
Identify top slow queries using EXPLAIN ANALYZE
Check for missing indexes
Review recent schema changes
Analyze query execution plans
remediation_steps: Add missing indexes for frequently queried columns
Rewrite inefficient queries
Add query caching where appropriate
Increase database server resources temporarily
Partition large tables if needed
rollback: Revert index changes or schema modifications
success_criteria: Slow query log shows no queries over 1 second

name: Bad Deployment Rollback
description: Roll back a failed or problematic deployment
diagnostic_steps: Confirm the deployment is the cause: check deployment timestamp vs incident start
Review deployment diff: git diff <prev-tag> <current-tag>
Check error logs for new error types post-deployment
Verify health checks and readiness probes
remediation_steps: Rollback immediately: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>
Verify rollback completed: kubectl rollout status deployment/<name>
Monitor service metrics for 5 minutes post-rollback
Notify engineering team of the rollback
Create incident ticket to track the bad deployment fix
rollback: If rollback fails, scale to zero and redeploy last known good version
success_criteria: Error rate returns to pre-deployment baseline
No new error types in logs

name: HTTP 5xx Investigation
description: Investigate and resolve HTTP 5xx error spikes
diagnostic_steps: Check error logs: filter by 5xx status codes
Identify which endpoints are returning errors
Check upstream service health (dependencies)
Review recent deployments
Check for configuration changes
remediation_steps: If dependency failure: enable circuit breaker or fallback
If deployment related: rollback deployment
If configuration error: revert configuration change
Restart unhealthy pods
Enable maintenance mode if error rate is critical
rollback: Restore previous application configuration and deployment
